text: [TACTICS] Work shoreline structure with lures like topwater, spinnerbaits, and jigs, casting under overhanging tree branches or next to deadfall. An effective technique boat or kayak anglers will often employ is fishing plastic worms over mid-lake structure and around the bridge pilings. You�ll also see kayak anglers slow-trolling crankbaits and lipped plugs through the lake. Shoreline anglers cast lures like crankbaits and spinnerbaits as well, although due to the limited mobility many will simply suspend a minnow under a bobber, cast it out, and wait for a bite.
[ACCESS] Free parking is available at the Austin High boat ramp. You can also put in a kayak or SUP at the Rowing Dock.

[TACTICS] Using ultralight spin-gear, cast the smallest possible crayfish soft plastic on a 1/32-1/16 oz jig. Smaller wacky rigs (4" or less) may also entice some larger fish to bite.  Small power grubs (white, chartreuse, or black) can also work for all species present in this water. For fly fishing, work a 5wt or lighter flyrod with a small bass bug, a blacktail shiner imitation such as the BC streamer, or a juvenile crawfish pattern such as the Rio Bandito should entice any of the variety of sunfish, cichlid and largemouth bass to bite. Be aware that the bass in Shoal Creek can be extremely spooky, so stealth is extremely important to your success.
